subject: ss-surgical-gastroenterology
title: Hernia abdominal wall and emergency surgery: inguinal ventral incisional strangulation and acute abdomen

steps.tx: **Inguinal hernia affects 27 percent of men** and 3 percent of women over life. Indirect sacs traverse the deep ring in 60 percent of cases. Direct hernias push through Hesselbach triangle in 40 percent. Strangulation occurs in 5 percent of neglected hernias within 5 years.
steps.say: Start hernia surgery with the lifetime risk that brings men to clinics far more often than women. Indirect sacs follow the cord through the deep ring, while direct sacs push straight through the floor. Neglect invites strangulation, so any irreducible painful hernia earns urgent assessment rather than routine listing.

steps.tx: Femoral hernia presents in **20 percent of women with groin hernias** and strangulates faster than inguinal types. Incarceration without vascular compromise occurs in 15 percent. Emergency femoral repair carries 10 percent mortality versus 1 percent elective. EHS size 1 to 3 classification guides mesh choice in 90 percent of ventral hernias.
steps.say: Imagine femoral hernias crouching under the inguinal ligament with narrow necks that trap bowel quickly. Women suffer this pattern disproportionately, and emergency repair carries far higher mortality than planned repair. Ventral defects scale from under one centimetre to over fifteen centimetres, and that width decides mesh overlap.

steps.tx: **Mesh repair reduces inguinal recurrence to 1 percent** versus 10 percent with suture alone. Lichtenstein repair keeps chronic groin pain under 5 percent. Laparoscopic repair cuts wound infection to 2 percent from 5 percent. Combined hydrocele repair is needed in 5 percent of recurrent inguinal cases.
steps.say: See how mesh has transformed groin repair through lower recurrence rather than faster surgery. Open mesh keeps nerve pain low, while keyhole approaches cut wound infection and speed return to work. Recurrent hernias with hydrocele need combined sac clearance to prevent seroma and recurrence.

steps.tx: **Ventral hernia recurrence reaches 20 percent** after suture repair in obese patients. Component separation clears 10 cm fascial width in 30 percent. Prehabilitation weight loss of 5 percent cuts recurrence to 10 percent. Mesh bridging without fascial closure fails in 25 percent by 3 years.
steps.say: Examine ventral recurrence through obesity and fascial width rather than through suture strength alone. Component separation gains precious centimetres of fascia, while modest weight loss before surgery measurably lowers failure. Bridging an open fascial gap without closure nearly always bulges within a few years.

steps.tx: **Strangulated hernia needs operating within 6 hours** to save bowel in 90 percent of early cases. Bowel necrosis appears after 8 hours in 40 percent of strangulated loops. Resection without anastomosis is safer in 20 percent with faecal peritonitis. Testicular atrophy follows 2 percent of emergency groin repairs.
steps.say: Check strangulated hernias for the clock that governs bowel survival hour by hour. Beyond eight hours necrosis climbs sharply, and faecal contamination forbids anastomosis. Emergency groin dissection threatens testicular blood supply, so atrophy awareness shapes consent and technique.

steps.tx: **Acute abdomen perforation shows free air in 70 percent** on erect chest X-ray. Blunt splenic injury grade 3 appears in 10 percent and needs angioembolisation. AAST grade 5 splenic injury kills 20 percent without surgery. Penetrating injury under 2 cm needs exploration in 60 percent of cases.
steps.say: Discuss acute abdomen through free air, organ grade, and mechanism rather than through pain alone. Erect chest films catch free subdiaphragmatic air in most perforations, while splenic grades decide between embolisation and operation. Penetrating wounds with short tracts still need exploration when peritoneal signs appear.

steps.tx: **Abdominal trauma mortality reaches 15 percent** in blunt injury with 40 percent from haemorrhage. Damage control laparotomy packs succeed in 60 percent of coagulopathic cases. Whole body CT shortens diagnostic time to under 30 minutes. Fascia closure delay beyond 5 days needs mesh in 30 percent.
steps.say: Review trauma mortality for the haemorrhage fraction that damage control aims to interrupt. Packing controls venous bleeding while correction of clotting proceeds in intensive care. Whole body scanning accelerates decisions, but open abdomens left beyond five days rarely close primarily.

steps.tx: **Acute appendicitis peaks at 20 years** with migration of pain in 70 percent before localisation. Alvarado score above 7 predicts appendicitis in 80 percent. Nonoperative antibiotics succeed in 70 percent without surgery. Interval appendicectomy is needed in 20 percent for recurrent symptoms within 12 months.
steps.say: Distinguish appendicitis migration from visceral pain that settles as the inflamed appendix touches the parietal wall. Scoring systems combine tenderness, leukocytosis, and fever to sort surgical from medical care. Antibiotics alone settle most early cases, but recurrence pushes many toward interval surgery later.

steps.tx: **Adhesive small bowel obstruction settles in 70 percent** without operation within 72 hours. Water soluble contrast predicts nonoperative success in 85 percent. Closed loop strangulation complicates 10 percent and needs surgery now. CT whirl sign appears in 30 percent of volvulus cases.
steps.say: Compare contrast follow through with plain films for adhesive obstruction triage. Most adhesions release within three days, while strangulated closed loops cannot wait for fluids alone. The whirl pattern on CT tells you the twist and the urgency more reliably than pain scores.

steps.tx: Complications include **wound infection in 8 percent after emergency laparotomy** and dehiscence in 2 percent. Intra abdominal collection follows 10 percent of perforation repairs. Enterocutaneous fistula develops in 5 percent of open abdomens. Secondary mesh hernias recur in 25 percent after delayed closure.
steps.say: Consider wound infection and bursting after emergency laparotomy, especially with contamination and obesity. Collections declare with fever after the third day and need image guided drainage. High output fistulas complicate open abdomens and demand nutritional support before any closure attempt.

steps.tx: **Mesh inguinal repair recurs in 1 percent** while strangulation needs 6 hour surgery to save 90 percent bowel. Ventral suture recurrence hits 20 percent and weight loss of 5 percent cuts it to 10 percent. Adhesive obstruction settles in 70 percent within 72 hours. Appendicitis Alvarado above 7 predicts 80 percent surgical need.
steps.say: High-yield for the exam, remember the mesh recurrence, the strangulation clock, and the adhesion settle rate. Ventral recurrence halves with modest weight loss before elective repair. Alvarado scoring above seven keeps you on the operative side in most young adults with migrating pain.
